terminal.name: Claude Code
terminal.verdict: The default harness in HN setup threads, often run through Desktop, Web or T3 Code. Praised for UX, skills and remote control; complaints are usage burn, ignored memory and unwanted files.

terminal.name: Codex CLI
terminal.what_it_is: OpenAI's terminal and desktop coding agent
terminal.verdict: Usually the second subscription beside Claude, kept for review and second opinions. Credited with solid one-shots and fast-moving desktop features; dinged for hitting limits, bugs and loud default design taste.

terminal.name: OpenCode
terminal.what_it_is: Open-source terminal coding agent, any model
terminal.verdict: The go-to open harness for DeepSeek, GLM or local models, often on the $10 OpenCode Go plan. Liked for per-agent model choice; a few moved on to Pi or T3 Code.

terminal.name: Pi
terminal.what_it_is: Minimal, hackable open-source coding agent harness
terminal.verdict: A lean harness people bend to their own workflows, often with local or open models and the oh-my-pi fork. Liked for small prompts that fit tight context windows.
terminal.notes: Several ids appear twice (ask_hn and hn_comment copies of the same comment).

terminal.name: Gemini CLI
terminal.what_it_is: Google's open-source terminal agent for Gemini
terminal.verdict: Older threads used it as the free option and liked its web search and code explanations. By late 2026 commenters call it deprecated for subscribers and replaced by Antigravity CLI.
terminal.notes: 5 false matches: Antigravity CLI mentions and a Gemini-protocol client.

terminal.name: Aider
terminal.what_it_is: Open-source terminal pair programmer, manual context
terminal.verdict: The pre-agent pair programmer, still liked by a few for manual file control and accuracy. Most commenters moved on, calling the manual context loading busywork next to agentic tools.
terminal.notes: Several neutral hits are the Ask HN question text quoted back; one points to the successor Cecli.

terminal.name: DeepSeek Harness
terminal.what_it_is: DeepSeek's own agent harness, desktop and TUI
terminal.verdict: A cheap home setup for many commenters, paired with DeepSeek Flash for a few dollars a month. Praised for speed, value and plugins; web search is the recurring weak spot.
terminal.notes: Many ids duplicated across ask_hn and hn_comment.

terminal.name: Goose
terminal.what_it_is: Block's open-source extensible agent, Linux Foundation
terminal.verdict: Block's open agent, now under the Linux Foundation, used for everyday tasks and custom bots. A few like its TUI; others found it too agentic or no better than prompting directly.
terminal.notes: 7 false matches: goose idioms, goose-neck microphone, Pygmy-Goose.

terminal.name: Copilot CLI
terminal.verdict: Used where work already pays for GitHub Copilot; users say it runs close to Claude Code on the same models. Complaints target Autopilot mode, token burn and a thin plugin system.

terminal.name: Qwen Code
terminal.what_it_is: Alibaba's terminal agent for Qwen models
terminal.verdict: Mostly paired with local Qwen models on home hardware. One user built a 3D game with it in two days; others found local runs slow and error-prone next to Claude Code.
terminal.notes: 6 false matches about Qwen Coder models rather than the CLI; thin direct evidence.

terminal.name: Muse Code
terminal.what_it_is: Meta's terminal agent for Muse models
terminal.verdict: Usually a cheap extra subscription next to Claude or Codex. One user relies on it for code review; others note tight limits on the top model or say they barely touch it.
terminal.notes: 7 neutral hits are the Ask HN question text quoted back; thin evidence.

terminal.name: Mistral Vibe
terminal.verdict: Mostly used as a cheap way to run hosted GLM-5.3. Fans call it fast and good enough; critics say the harness is sluggish, times out or ignores instructions.

terminal.name: Kimi CLI
terminal.what_it_is: Moonshot's open-source terminal agent for Kimi
terminal.verdict: Moonshot's harness for Kimi models, used by Kimi subscribers. Commenters credit its checkpoint rollback for taming Kimi's tool-call loops; one critic called it a copy of basic harnesses.

editors.name: Cursor
editors.what_it_is: AI-first VS Code fork with agents
editors.verdict: Often described as where commenters used to be. Usage limits and API-priced bills keep pushing people to a Claude subscription; a few still like its bundled plans.
editors.notes: 6 false matches: text cursors and terminal cursors.

editors.name: VS Code + Copilot
editors.what_it_is: GitHub Copilot agent inside VS Code
editors.verdict: Mostly the option work pays for. Praised for PR reviews, model choice and keep/undo diffs; others call it meh and dry next to Claude.
editors.notes: 1 false match: Microsoft 365 Copilot. Many neutral mentions of employer-provided seats.

editors.name: Zed
editors.what_it_is: Fast Rust editor with ACP agent support
editors.verdict: The editor many keep beside their agents, driving Claude or Codex over ACP or just reviewing code. Liked for speed and agent support; some found it overhyped or unusable without a GPU.

editors.name: Antigravity
editors.what_it_is: Google's agent IDE and CLI for Gemini
editors.verdict: The only subscription route to Gemini. Some use it daily for search and planning; complaints center on billing and account friction and a weak harness.

editors.name: Windsurf
editors.what_it_is: AI VS Code fork, team now at Google
editors.verdict: Mostly mentioned in the past tense now that its team went to Google. Older threads liked its codebase Q&A, autocomplete and parallel flows, but said it struggled on large files.
editors.notes: 1 false match (windsurfer). Recent mentions are mostly in tool lists or acquisition talk.

editors.name: Cline
editors.what_it_is: Open-source agent extension for VS Code
editors.verdict: Popular for pairing cheap API models like DeepSeek Flash, or local Ollama models, with VS Code. Liked for permission prompts and provider choice; several left after finding it slow and unstable.
editors.notes: Many ids duplicated across ask_hn and hn_comment.

editors.name: Kiro
editors.what_it_is: Amazon's spec-driven agentic VS Code fork
editors.verdict: Mostly a work-mandated tool at AWS shops. Its spec-driven workflow gets borrowed elsewhere; Amazon engineers say the harness trails Claude Code and degrades over long context.

editors.name: Neovim (CodeCompanion / avante)
editors.what_it_is: AI chat and edit plugins for Neovim
editors.verdict: Neovim users reach for CodeCompanion for in-editor chat and quick edits, handing bigger tasks to OpenCode or Claude Code. Local-model setups can loop, and completion trails Cursor Tab.
editors.notes: 10 false matches: generic Neovim mentions and mcp-neovim-server, not the plugins.

editors.name: Roo Code
editors.what_it_is: Cline fork for VS Code, now discontinued
editors.verdict: Ran on your own API key or local models inside VS Code. Users liked its control, visible costs and architect and orchestrator modes; it has been discontinued, with forks carrying on.
editors.notes: Project shut down; much praise is from 2025 threads.

editors.name: Kilo Code
editors.what_it_is: Roo Code fork for VS Code, JetBrains
editors.verdict: Run on your own keys or Kilo credits across many models. Users say it gets the job done; gripes are weak compaction and a recent version that feels blander.
editors.notes: 3 hits are from a Kilo maintainer disclosing affiliation.

editors.name: JetBrains Junie
editors.what_it_is: JetBrains' coding agent inside its IDEs
editors.verdict: Popular with IntelliJ users, often paired with cheap Gemini Flash. Good for small, well-defined tasks and tests; quotas are tight and some rate the harness below Claude Code.

editors.name: Continue
editors.what_it_is: Open-source VS Code assistant, now end-of-life
editors.verdict: Was the usual way to plug Ollama or LM Studio models into VS Code. Now end-of-life after Cursor bought it; one user found it broken regardless of model.
editors.notes: Most recent mentions are about the acquisition and shutdown.

editors.name: Emacs gptel
editors.what_it_is: LLM client and agent toolkit for Emacs
editors.verdict: Built for human-in-the-loop work: chat, code review and questions inside Emacs. Praised for staying out of the way and tiny token bills; agentic features are mostly do-it-yourself.

orchestration.name: Herdr
orchestration.what_it_is: Terminal workspace for many agent sessions
orchestration.verdict: Runs several Claude Code, Codex or Pi sessions side by side. Loved for agent-done pings and a pane overview; a few never clicked with it or switched to Rex.

orchestration.name: tmux + git worktrees
orchestration.what_it_is: DIY parallel agents with tmux, worktrees
orchestration.verdict: The do-it-yourself baseline: a worktree per task, a tmux pane per agent, send-keys for messages. Fans say the new agent IDEs only repackage it; many build their own wrappers on top.
orchestration.notes: Generic pattern, so many snippets are about third-party tools built on it.

orchestration.name: Gas Town
orchestration.verdict: On HN it is mostly a punchline: called too complex, too opinionated and a token sink, with nobody running evals against a plain harness. A few tried it for experiments.

orchestration.name: Paseo
orchestration.what_it_is: Open-source desktop and mobile agent interface
orchestration.verdict: A front end for Pi, Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode agents. Liked for its phone app and client-server setup; reports of memory strain and hung sub-agent status updates.

orchestration.name: Beads
orchestration.what_it_is: Git-backed issue tracker for coding agents
orchestration.verdict: Gives agents epics, tasks and dependencies to pull from, and some teams run their whole backlog on it. Critics call it bloated and question why it needs a daemon and database.

orchestration.name: T3 Code
orchestration.what_it_is: Open-source GUI driving multiple agent harnesses
orchestration.verdict: Drives Claude Code, Codex and Pi from one UI across machines. Fans praise mid-conversation agent handoff and remote sessions; others found it buggy or heavy on resources.

orchestration.name: Conductor
orchestration.what_it_is: Mac app for parallel worktree agents, closing
orchestration.verdict: Ran Claude and Codex in parallel git worktrees and is now shutting down. Users liked it for mid-size tasks and review; complaints were weak multi-repo support and Mac-only builds.
orchestration.notes: 3 false matches (superconductor, semiconductor). One positive hit is from the creator.

orchestration.name: Orca
orchestration.what_it_is: Open-source agent IDE for worktrees, remote
orchestration.verdict: Often self-hosted, with a mobile app for steering agents away from the desk. Praised for remote SSH and multi-worktree views; one user hit install trouble on a headless server.
orchestration.notes: One hit is from the Orca team.

orchestration.name: Juggler
orchestration.what_it_is: GUI coding agent from JUCE's creator
orchestration.verdict: Treats local and remote sessions the same, which suits cross-platform work. Users like the control and visibility; one found its nested output stressful, another wished it were less vibecoded.
orchestration.notes: 4 hits are from the creator; 3 false matches (Amiga Juggler, juggling).

orchestration.name: Ralph loop
orchestration.verdict: A pattern, not a product: rerun the agent until the task list says done. Used for overnight PR polishing and test coverage; skeptics call it token burning that hides broken tests.

orchestration.name: Sculptor
orchestration.what_it_is: Imbue's desktop UI for Claude Code
orchestration.verdict: A desktop UI for running Claude Code agents. The scraped comments are almost all about actual sculptors, so there are no recent user reports to summarize.
orchestration.notes: 12 of 13 snippets are false matches; no usable sentiment evidence.

orchestration.name: Vibe Kanban
orchestration.what_it_is: Kanban board that dispatches coding agents
orchestration.verdict: Users liked managing agents across projects from one board, but its developers stopped investing in it, and some felt it added little to their productivity.

orchestration.name: Omnara
orchestration.what_it_is: Remote and API layer for coding agents
orchestration.verdict: Began as phone and web remote control for Claude Code and Codex, now pitched as a self-hostable agent API. One user relies on it in transit; another found alternatives more reliable.
orchestration.notes: Most snippets are from the founder or builders; little user evidence.
